title: Dizzy leaves in January 1945; Fats Navarro replaces him
summary: Dizzy goes out on his own, and the 21-year-old, very heavy Fats Navarro comes in on his recommendation.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I've talked about Art Blakely (sic) and about Charlie... I was trying to think about some of the other members of the band...

Well, Fats came in the band after Dizzy. Dizzy stayed with the band until January of 1945. By this time, he felt like he was strong enough to do some things on his own. He had offers from agents in New York to do things. I guess, name-wise, he was the most popular instrumentalist in the band. Because Dizzy had been around for a while, he had played with a lot of bands and he'd made quite a few records with different people, and he was a well-known musician.

So Dizzy left the band in January of 1945, and we got this trumpet player who had been formerly with Andy Kirk's band. Of course, he had played with other bands before -- Snookum Russell. But he came with us not long after he had left Andy Kirk's band. His name was Fats Navarro -- at least,

that's what everyone used to call him, because he was extremely fat. I don't know how much Fats weighed, but it must have been close to 300 pounds that he weighed, and he was a young man -- Fats was only 21 years old. He was an excellent trumpet player, and it was Dizzy's recommendation that they get him for the band.
